title: TNA SP 106/10: a codebreaker's file of Italian intercepts and worksheets, c. 1623-24 (DECODE R657, R660, R664, R704, R720, R721, R722; key R725; worksheets R658, R661, R663, R667, R684, R701, R702, R703)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE metadata for R657, R660, R664, R704, R720, R721 and the pointers; identified the seventh record as R722 and a key record R725 in the same run of shelfmarks. Downloaded all 28 images with the project cookie.

Read DECODE R725, 'The Alphabett of Single Letters' - the contemporary codebreaker's fair key: a 20-value letter alphabet, a list of single letters standing for whole words, and two nomenclator word-lists.

Identified from the key sheet's own note ('It seemes there are numbers of woordes expressed by this difference of - over the figures') that a bar and a dot over a two-figure group select two different word-lists.

Dated the group from the recovered nomenclature - Marques Inichiosa (the Marques de la Inojosa, ambassador in England 1623-24), Palatinato, Il Principe, C. Barberino, Papa, Nuncio, Imbassiatore di Venetia - against DECODE's date, which is only the volume span 1558/1625.

Surveyed all 22 ciphertext pages and found they use three different systems, not one: R657 (two-figure), R660/R664/R720 (three-figure), R704/R721/R722 (letter-plus-figure). DECODE groups R720 with R704; the figures show it belongs with R660/R664.

Rebuilt about 45 values of the three-figure code (system B) by aligning the codebreaker's interlinear syllables against the groups on R664 f. 1, anchored on unambiguous words ('senza', 'della loro sicurezza', 'quelle de nuovo').

Checked the rebuilt values for consistency across lines 34-45; the apparent conflict at 252/359 resolved when 'senza' was seen to run over a line break (252 se + 359 n + 560 za), which confirms the alignment method.
Web search for any modern edition of SP 106/10; the published SP 106 transcription site covers only volumes 1-4, and nothing else was found.
Catalogue entry 66 (DECODE R703, ff. 184-185) taken up; fetched its two images and those of the neighbouring records R658, R661, R667, R684, R701, R702.

Tested whether R703's glossed fragments and group-by-line index belong to R664, R660 or the system-C letters R704/R721-R724. They do not: they come from a fourth, three-figure letter of 46 lines not among the DECODE images, worked also on R661, R667, R684, R701, R702 and R720.

Read the codebreaker's partial key for that letter on R701 p.3 (syllabary: 209-213 va-vu, 231-235 sa-su, 333-336 cha-cho, 366-370 la-lu, 375-378 da-do) and his label on R701 p.1, 'Wordes marked wth letters in the Venetian Cifar'.

Applied the partial key to the fragments on R703, R702, R684 and R720: it values 4 of R703's 28 groups and contradicts the codebreaker's own glosses (244 ta/ra). No reading; R703 closed as explained, not read.
Catalogue 62: fetched DECODE metadata and all 17 images of R658, R661, R663, R667, R684, R701, R702 (and R725 again) with the project cookie.

Surveyed the seven records: all are the same codebreaker's worksheets, none an intercept; R658 is his grid of the three-figure code with counts and values, R667 a count grid of a second three-figure code (system D).
Read R701 p.1 'Wordes marked with letters in the Venetian Cifer' (369 nostro, 467 questo, 430 passata) and matched it to R658's side list: the three-figure code of R664/R660 is the 'Venetian Cifer'.

Transcribed the R658 grid and rebuilt system B as a systematic syllabary (consonant x a-e-i-o-u in five rows, one consonant per hundreds column): 117 values, 102 written by the codebreaker, 15 predicted from the pattern (cat62/venetian_code.tsv).

Decoded the group strings the codebreaker glossed on R702 p.2 with the rebuilt table (cat62/check_r702.py): 46/46 groups covered, each string giving his gloss (i colonelli, della loro, sendosi, conservarsi, che possiamo prometter, in tanto).
Compared with the 2026-09-20 gloss-alignment values from R664: 260, 262, 263 and 459 were wrong (ta, ti, to, r, not mento, to, ti, v) and are corrected.
Annealed a one-to-one substitution on the short letter cipher of R701 p.2 (about 110 letters) against Italian, English, Spanish, French and Latin 4-gram models (cat62/mono701.py).
The second three-figure code (groups 200-599, key on R701 p.3) belongs to the lost 46-line letter identified the same day from R703; only line fragments survive, so it was not attempted further here.
Catalogue 58: fetched DECODE metadata and images for R656, R662, R722, R931 and neighbours (R655, R657, R663, R930, R932); R931 and R932 carry DECODE transcriptions, R932 also Lasry's key.

Looked at R722 for the first time: not system C but the second three-figure code; line 1 '540 212 una di questi matine' = R703's quoted 'l.1 540 212 una che', and five more worksheet fragments match. It is the '46-line intercept' earlier sessions thought unimaged.

Read R722's endorsement 'Cypher of a Venetian Secretary to the Embassador of that nation in ...' and the clear passages (Spinola sotto Breda, di Bruselles si e inteso, V. E.); dated to the first half of 1625 by the Breda siege.
R656: English Exchequer draft reused for line-numbered group strings; l.12 '313 541 377 238 254' is R722 line 12 verbatim. Worksheet on R722.
R662: strip of the codebreaker's English memorandum on the code (series of syllables, vowels a.e.i for every consonant, 'most frequent ... di'); not a letter.
R931 (Sept 1645, 104 distinct numbers in 192): applied Lasry's TNA SP 106, SP106-2, SP106-5, SP106-8 keys and the R932 Goring key.

R931: compared with Charles I to Culpeper 1645 key (BL Add MS 32256 ff. 6-7, DECODE R9117/R9118): words 300-600, nothing in 100-260; does not fit. R9116 (Charles I to the Queen, Oxford 1642) is only a frequency tally with no values and R9119 f. 8 a blank ruled sheet.
R722 transcribed in full from the images: 48 lines, 420 groups, 117 types, clear passages (Bethune, Pontifice, 150 m, Spinola sotto Breda).
Line 24 'che 525 245 541 449 lo haveva' = 'che il Re glie-lo haveva'; line 8 '245 510 Almeno' = 'resta'; confirms R701 p.3's table (244 ra, 245 re, 510 sta, 333-336 cha-cho) for this letter.
Simulated annealing of the remaining ~70 groups against it-cinquecento, four configurations (free; length-normalised; R701 values fixed; plus run-of-five prior), 12-20 restarts each.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary codebreaker's own key sheet DECODE R725 and his grid R658 of the 'Venetian Cifer', filed in the same SP 106/10 file, gave the values; the first ~45 three-figure values were aligned from his interlinear glosses on R664.
outcome.notes: The case is explained and dated and system A's key is fully transcribed; system B is read in fragments from a partly rebuilt code. Systems B and C are not yet carried to a continuous reading, and no sender or recipient is yet named. R703 (catalogue 66, 2026-09-21) is a worksheet on a fourth, lost Venetian-cipher letter worked on seven records; that letter is explained, not read. Catalogue 62 (2026-09-21): the codebreaker's grid R658 rebuilds the three-figure code of R664/R660 as a systematic syllabary (117 values) and corrects four values; the lost 46-line letter's code (R701 p.3) is a different table. fraction_read is an estimate from the NOTES (share of cipher tokens given a value), not measured.

gaps.item: R664 ff. 1-3 and R660 (system B, the Venetian code) continuous reading
gaps.detail: code rebuilt to 117 values from R658, the letters never decoded through with it

gaps.item: R704, R721, R722 (system C letter-plus-figure syllabary)
gaps.detail: the codebreaker's interlinear solutions exist, no alignment pass done

gaps.item: R657 worksheets (system A) against key R725
lost 46-line intercept of the second three-figure code (fragments on R667, R684, R701 p.3, R702 p.1, R703)
gaps.detail: the intercept is not among the imaged records, perhaps elsewhere in SP 106/10 or SP 99 at Kew
about 120 letters, simple-substitution annealing in five languages gave nothing

outcome.fraction_read_source: no continuous reading file for R660/R664/R704/R721/R722; only phrases in NOTES prose and the code table cat62/venetian_code.tsv

prior.where: the contemporary English codebreaker's own partial solutions, written interlinearly on the intercepts themselves and summarised as a key on DECODE R725; no modern edition (the published SP 106 transcriptions cover only SP 106/1-4)

human: nothing beyond setting the target; images fetched with the project DECODE cookie
